modules.title: Transportation and Communication
modules.html:
Transportation

Transport creates place utility by moving goods and people from where they are less needed to where they are more needed.

ModeAdvantagesDisadvantages
RoadFlexible, door-to-door, cheap for short distanceAccidents, congestion, small loads
RailCheap for heavy bulky goods over long distance, safeInflexible, fixed routes, high capital cost
WaterCheapest for very bulky international cargoVery slow; ports required
AirFastest; ideal for perishables and valuablesMost expensive; limited capacity; weather-dependent
PipelineContinuous, low running cost for liquids and gasOnly for fluids; vandalism; high initial cost
Factors Determining Choice of Transport
  1. Nature and value of the goods
  2. Urgency and perishability
  3. Distance and route availability
  4. Cost of carriage relative to value
  5. Safety and level of risk

Communication

Communication removes the barrier of ignorance. Types: oral, written, visual and electronic. Modern services include mobile telephony, e-mail, video conferencing, internet banking, courier services and the postal system (registered mail, PO Box, money order).

Importance
  • Speeds up orders, quotations and payment.
  • Links branches and enables management control.
  • Provides market information and price data.
  • Supports e-commerce and remote work.

examples.q: A trader must move 20 tonnes of tomatoes from Jos to Lagos. Road haulage costs ₦320,000 with 12% spoilage; air freight costs ₦900,000 with 1% spoilage. Tomatoes sell for ₦120,000 per tonne. Which is better?
examples.a: Road: revenue \(=20\times0.88\times120{,}000=₦2{,}112{,}000\); less ₦320,000 → ₦1,792,000. Air: revenue \(=20\times0.99\times120{,}000=₦2{,}376{,}000\); less ₦900,000 → ₦1,476,000. Road transport yields ₦316,000 more, so it is preferable despite higher spoilage.

examples.q: State three ways ICT has changed Nigerian commerce.
examples.a: Mobile money and internet banking have replaced much cash handling; online marketplaces let small traders reach nationwide customers without a shop; instant messaging and e-mail reduce the cost and delay of placing orders and confirming shipments.

modules.title: Warehousing
modules.html:
Meaning

Warehousing is the holding and storing of goods from the time of production until they are needed, creating time utility and steadying prices.

Types of Warehouse

  1. Wholesaler's warehouse – stores bulk goods for breaking down.
  2. Retailer's warehouse – small stockroom attached to a shop.
  3. Manufacturer's warehouse – raw materials and finished goods.
  4. Bonded warehouse – dutiable imports held under customs control.
  5. Public/dock warehouse – rented space, often at ports.
  6. Cold store – refrigerated storage for perishables.

Functions

  • Protects goods from theft, weather and deterioration.
  • Ensures steady supply and stable prices throughout the year.
  • Allows grading, blending, packaging and branding.
  • Enables bulk purchase and quantity discounts.
  • Facilitates deferment of import duty (bonded).

Factors in Siting a Warehouse

Nearness to market and to transport routes, security, cost of land, availability of power and labour, nature of goods, and expansion possibilities.

Storage Cost Illustration

Total storage cost \( = \text{Fixed rent} + (\text{Rate per unit per month} \times \text{units} \times \text{months}) \).

examples.q: A warehouse charges ₦80,000 fixed monthly rent plus ₦150 per bag per month. A trader stores 900 bags for 3 months. Find the total cost and cost per bag.
Explain how warehousing stabilises prices of seasonal produce.
examples.a: At harvest, supply is abundant and prices would crash; storing part of the crop reduces the quantity on the market. In the off-season, the stored goods are released, preventing extreme scarcity and price spikes. Prices are thus evened out over the year.

modules.title: Advertising and Other Aids
modules.html:
Meaning and Types

Advertising is any paid, non-personal presentation of goods, services or ideas by an identified sponsor.

  • Informative advertising – gives facts about a new product.
  • Persuasive/competitive advertising – urges the buyer to prefer one brand.
  • Collective/generic advertising – sponsored by an industry to promote a whole product class.

Media

MediumStrengthWeakness
TelevisionSight, sound and motion; wide reachVery expensive
RadioCheap; reaches rural and local-language audiencesNo visual impact
Newspaper/magazineDetailed, can be kept for referenceOnly literate audience
Outdoor (billboards)Repeated exposure; low cost per viewBrief message only
Social media/internetTargeted, measurable, interactiveRequires data access; ad fatigue

Advantages and Criticisms

Advantages: creates awareness and demand, supports mass production and lower unit cost, finances the media, aids new product launches, informs about prices and quality.
Criticisms: raises the price of goods, may mislead, encourages wasteful/impulse buying, promotes materialism, and can create harmful brand monopoly.

Other Aids to Trade

  • Banking – finance, payment and safekeeping.
  • Insurance – transfer of risk.
  • Tourism – earns foreign exchange, creates employment and markets local products.

examples.q: A firm spends ₦3,000,000 on adverts and sales rise from ₦40,000,000 to ₦52,000,000 with a gross margin of 30%. Was the campaign worthwhile?
examples.a: Additional sales \(=₦12{,}000{,}000\); additional gross profit \(=30\%\times12{,}000{,}000=₦3{,}600{,}000\). Since ₦3,600,000 > ₦3,000,000 advertising cost, the campaign added ₦600,000 net – it was worthwhile, though other causes of the sales rise should be checked.

examples.q: Distinguish informative from persuasive advertising with examples.
examples.a: Informative advertising states facts – e.g. a bank announcing new USSD codes and branch addresses. Persuasive advertising appeals to emotion and comparison – e.g. a soft-drink advert claiming its taste is superior and showing happy young celebrities.

quiz.solution: Moving goods to where they are needed creates place utility.

quiz.q: The cheapest means of carrying very bulky goods over long international distances is
quiz.solution: Sea transport has the lowest cost per tonne-kilometre for bulk cargo.

quiz.q: Pipeline transport is most suitable for
quiz.solution: Only fluids and gases can flow through pipelines.
Holding goods until they are needed creates time utility.

quiz.q: A warehouse under customs control is called
quiz.solution: Dutiable goods stay there until duty is paid or they are re-exported.

quiz.q: Which factor is LEAST important in siting a warehouse?
quiz.solution: Aesthetics of the roof have no economic bearing on warehouse location.
It informs buyers about goods, prices and where to find them.

quiz.q: An advert sponsored by an entire industry is
quiz.solution: Generic adverts promote a product class, e.g. 'Drink more milk'.

quiz.q: A major criticism of advertising is that it
quiz.solution: Advertising costs are recovered in the selling price.

quiz.q: Which medium reaches rural, non-literate audiences best?
quiz.solution: Radio needs no literacy and is inexpensive and widespread.
Speed suits perishables and high-value light goods.

quiz.q: Communication in business is important because it
quiz.solution: Fast information flow shortens the order-to-payment cycle.

quiz.q: Storing goods at harvest and releasing them later helps to
quiz.solution: Even distribution across the year prevents extreme price swings.
Visitors spend foreign currency and create local employment.

quiz.q: Which mode is most flexible for door-to-door delivery?
quiz.solution: Road vehicles can reach almost any address.
